text: On perdurantism (worm theory), how do ordinary objects persist through time?
choices: By being wholly present at each moment of their existence
By existing only in the present, so that earlier stages have ceased to exist
By having distinct temporal parts, or stages, at each moment they exist, just as they have distinct spatial parts across their spatial extent
By an objective present that illuminates exactly one stage at a time
explanation: Perdurantism (worm theory) holds that an object is a four-dimensional whole with a distinct temporal part at each time it exists, mirroring the way it has different spatial parts across space; this dissolves the problem of temporary intrinsics by assigning incompatible properties to different stages. Option 0 states endurantism, its direct rival; option 1 folds in presentism; option 3 imports the moving-spotlight theory. Only option 2 gives the temporal-parts account.
